business_scope.primary_industry_name: Vertical Industrial ERP and Customer Relationship Software

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Switzerland (federal level; Canton of Zug intended for the registered seat and commercial register)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (codified Continental legal system; company law governed by the Swiss Code of Obligations, SR 220; AML/CFT and UBO transparency framework codified in federal statutes, implementing ordinances and FINMA circulars; Federal Supreme Court jurisprudence provides binding interpretation)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: EFTA Convention (Switzerland is a founding EFTA member state)
Switzerland-European Union Free Trade Agreement of 22 July 1972 (in force since 1 January 1973)
Switzerland-European Union Agreement on the Free Movement of Persons of 21 June 1999 (in force since 1 June 2002)
Switzerland-China BIT signed 1982, entered into force 1986; Switzerland-China FTA of 6 July 2013 (in force 1 July 2014)
Switzerland-United Arab Emirates BIT of 1998 (in force 1999)
Switzerland-United States DTA of 1996, as amended by Protocol of 2009 (in force 23 September 2011)
Switzerland-Germany DTA of 1971, as amended (in force 1972)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal Act on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (AMLA), SR 955.0, as last revised by the 2023 AML enforcement package (in force 1 January 2023); FINMA Anti-Money Laundering Ordinance (AMLO-FINMA), SR 955.033; Swiss Criminal Code (SR 311.0), Articles 305bis and 305ter; Swiss Code of Obligations (OR/CO), SR 220, Articles 620-763 (stock company / Aktiengesellschaft), Articles 621 and 632 (minimum capital and paid-up minimum), Article 626 (statutory seat), Article 950 (accuracy of corporate name); Swiss Civil Code, SR 210, Articles 52-59 (legal personality); UBO transparency and beneficial-owner register duties introduced by the Federal Act on the Implementation of the Revised Recommendations of the FATF of 27 September 2019 (in force 1 November 2020) and by the revised Ordinance on the Commercial Register (ORC/HRA), SR 221.411 (rev. 1 July 2020); relevant non-public UBO reporting duties effective 1 January 2023 under the AML reinforcement act.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport of each shareholder, ultimate beneficial owner and member of the board of directors
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport-issuing authority of the holder's country of origin (e.g., U.S. Department of State, EU national registries, Swiss federal population register)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (1961 Convention) or Consular Legalization for non-member countries

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original notarized Power of Attorney (special proxy authorizing the Swiss notary and register office to incorporate the AG)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the jurisdiction of the grantor

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency / Certificate of Good Standing / extract of foreign commercial register (for any corporate shareholder)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry of the shareholder's domicile (e.g., U.S. Secretary of State, Companies House, Hong Kong Companies Registry, FSCA South Africa)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank or practicing accountant reference letter including source-of-funds declaration for the paid-up share capital
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed bank or certified public accountant of the contributing shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy; Hague Apostille on the signer's signature where required

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory customer due diligence before establishment of the mandate in accordance with AMLA Articles 3-6 and AMLO-FINMA: identify and verify all shareholders, directors and ultimate beneficial owners; determine PEP status (politically exposed persons under AMLA Article 2a paragraph 1, including family members and close associates) and apply enhanced due diligence where such status exists; mandatory screening against the Swiss SECO consolidated sanctions list, the United Nations Security Council sanctions regimes as implemented in SR 946.203, the OFAC SDN list (Swiss bank market standard), the EU consolidated financial sanctions list and the Swiss Ordinance on Measures against Money Laundering (SR 946.201); ongoing transaction and financing monitoring required under AMLA Article 6; for the targeted low-risk ISIC 6201 vertical ERP/CRM cloud software activity no statutory license is required, but the AG must contract a licensed Swiss payment services provider for the Stripe Billing and Direct Debit rails and must not itself engage in regulated financial services.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: ZEFIX - Central Business Name Index of Switzerland (www.zefix.ch), maintained by the Federal Commercial Register Office within the Federal Office of Justice; the name reservation application is filed through the Cantonal Commercial Register Office of the intended seat (target: Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug) with co-signature of a public notary.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name (Firma) must be expressed in an official Swiss language (German, French or Italian) in Latin alphabet characters; the name must close with the statutory legal-form indicator 'Aktiengesellschaft' or 'AG' (German) or 'Societe Anonyme' / 'SA' (French and Italian); non-Latin script names (e.g., Chinese, Cyrillic, Arabic) must be transliterated into Latin characters with certified transliteration attached; an English-composed name (e.g., 'Vertical Cloud ERP AG') is admissible provided it is not misleading under Article 950 CO and shows a genuine connection to the business (ISIC 6201 software); the distinctiveness of the name is examined within the same business branch in ZEFIX and against zone and trademark registrations.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Banque, Bankier and any term implying banking activity (requires FINMA banking license)
Versicherung, Assurance and insurance-related terms (requires FINMA insurance license)
Fonds, Fund and collective investment scheme terms (requires FINMA license under CISA)
Audit, Revisionsstelle, Wirtschaftspruefer and audit terms (reserved to licensed audit firms under RAB/ASR)
Rechtsanwalt, Anwalt, Avocat and legal-practice terms (reserved to licensed attorneys)
Treuhand, Fiduciaire, Fiduciary (subject to enhanced scrutiny and substance verification)
Swiss, Suisse, Svizzera, Schweiz and the Swiss cross (protected under Swissness legislation and the emblem protection act)
Eidgenossenschaft, Bund, Confederation, Nationalbank and other official public-authority terms
Zug (protected cantonal name; requires cantonal consent or a genuine local establishment)
Bourse, Boerse and stock-exchange terms implying regulated trading venue activity
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name is rejected, the Cantonal Commercial Register Office issues a written refusal with grounds; the applicant may file an administrative appeal within 30 days of notification to the cantonal supervisory authority for commercial register matters (Article 24 ORC/HRA); further appeal lies to the Federal Administrative Court and, where statutory conditions are met, to the Federal Supreme Court; in parallel, the applicant may at any time submit a new name reservation application with a modified name, after re-running the preliminary ZEFIX availability search; appeal and refiling costs are typically absorbed in the notary's incorporation mandate or billed at the prevailing hourly benchmark.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht / Code des obligations), Arts. 620–763 (Aktiengesellschaft); Commercial Register Ordinance (HRegV, SR 221.411) and associated Federal Notary Law (Art. 55 SchKG).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt / Office du registre du commerce) of the canton of the registered office, co-supervised by the Federal Commercial Register Office (EHRA/FEDRO, Bern).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized deed of incorporation (Errichtungsurkunde / acte constitutif) with certified Articles of Association (Statuten / Statuts), submitted as the Application for Registration (Anmeldung / réquisition).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital CHF 100,000; at least 50% (CHF 50,000) must be paid up in cash before registration. Funds must be held in a blocked escrow account (Sperrkonto / compte bloqué) at a FINMA-licensed Swiss bank until the Commercial Register confirms registration; the bank's release confirmation is a mandatory filing exhibit. In-kind contributions require an audit report and certified opening balance sheet.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY] AG, adopted by written resolution under Art. 713 of the Swiss Code of Obligations. The Board resolves: (1) to confirm the subscription of founder shares and payment of share capital; (2) to approve CHF 50,000 released from the CHF 100,000 blocked escrow account at [Bank]; (3) to adopt the registered office at [Address], Switzerland; (4) to appoint [Name] as Chairman, [Name] as CEO with individual signature authority, and [Name] as CFO with joint signature authority; (5) to authorize the Chairman and CEO to execute and file all Commercial Register registrations and to appoint a statutory auditor if required. Unanimously adopted and binding.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Notarized Deed of Incorporation and Articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Notary (Notariat / Étude notariale) in the canton of the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Association and incorporation deed in accordance with Arts. 620–642 CO. Verify the identity and legal capacity of all founding shareholders. Execute the public deed before the notary, who certifies the founders' signatures and the capital structure, then forwards the deed and capital exhibits to the Commercial Register.
required_dossiers: Notarized deed of incorporation
Signed Articles of Association (Statuten / Statuts)
Valid passports or identification documents of all founding shareholders and board members
Notarized power of attorney if any founder signs by proxy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary queries capital or shareholder data, correct the deed by amendment, re-notarize, and re-submit; no registry penalty applies if corrected before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establishment of Blocked Escrow Capital Account and Bank Capital Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: FINMA-licensed Swiss bank (e.g., cantonal bank or private bank) selected by the founders.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked capital account in the name of 'Company AG in formation' and deposit at least CHF 50,000. Instruct the bank to issue a formal capital confirmation (Kapitalbestätigung / attestation de libération) stating the deposited amount, the account holder, and the blocked status until Commercial Register registration is evidenced.
required_dossiers: Bank account opening application
Draft Articles of Association and company name reservation confirmation
Identity and economic beneficial owner declarations for all shareholders
Source-of-funds statement and banking background information
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires enhanced AML documentation, provide a corporate structure chart, origin-of-wealth evidence, and a legal opinion confirming the lawful source of funds; select an alternative FINMA-licensed bank if delays persist.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Incorporation Application with the Cantonal Commercial Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt / Office du registre du commerce) of the canton of the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized deed, Articles of Association, bank capital confirmation, list of directors and authorized signatories, and corporate governance declarations via the electronic register portal or paper filing. Pay the official filing fee to the cantonal registry and monitor the application status.
required_dossiers: Notarized deed of incorporation and Articles of Association
Bank capital confirmation letter from the escrow account
List of board members and authorized signatories with specimen signatures
Declaration confirming no undisclosed shareholders or non-audited in-kind contributions
Consent forms for any director domicile outside Switzerland (name of Swiss representative, if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a query (Nachtrag / réquisition), respond in writing within 10 working days, correct the Articles or signatures, and have the notary re-certify the amendment for electronic re-submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB) and Constitutive Effect
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (Schweizerisches Handelsamtsblatt – SHAB / Feuille officielle suisse du commerce – FOSC), operated by the Confederation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the Commercial Register entry is completed, the registry transmits the filing to SHAB for mandatory publication. Legal personality of the AG arises upon the completed entry and publication. Obtain a certified Commercial Register extract (Handelsregisterauszug) and verify the SHAB entry number and publication date.
required_dossiers: Certified Commercial Register extract
SHAB publication receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the SHAB publication contains clerical errors, file a correction request with the Commercial Register via the notary; rectification is administrative and does not affect the constitutive validity of the registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Tax, Social Security, and Occupational Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/AFC) for VAT and direct federal tax; cantonal tax administration; cantonal compensation fund (Ausgleichskasse) for AHV/AVS; SUVA for occupational accident insurance; State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO) for labor law compliance.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 30 days of registration, apply for VAT registration if annual taxable turnover is expected to exceed CHF 250,000 (mandatory) or elect voluntary VAT; register as an employer with the compensation fund for social security (AHV/IV/EO); register with mandatory accident insurers; complete the EKAS/SUVA occupational safety self-declaration for office workplaces.
required_dossiers: Certified Commercial Register extract
Articles of Association and board resolution on tax registration
Employee wage and social security registration forms
Lease agreement for the registered office
Identification and tax declarations of directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If VAT registration is back-dated or queried, apply for retroactive registration under Art. 55 VAT Act with supporting turnover projections; social security disputes are appealable to the competent cantonal insurance authority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Activation of Operational Bank Account and Payment Rail Integration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Swiss bank and payment service providers (Stripe Billing and Direct Debit / LSV+ or B2B clearing through SEPA).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convert the blocked escrow account into a fully operational current account. Request CHF/EUR IBANs and activate domestic and SEPA payment rails. Integrate Stripe Billing for recurring CRM subscriptions and Direct Debit mandates under the AG's treasury policy. Complete FATCA/CRS self-certification for all shareholders and beneficial owners.
required_dossiers: Certified Commercial Register extract and Articles of Association
Board resolution approving banking signatories and payment rail providers
FATCA/CRS self-certification forms
AML questionnaire and source-of-funds evidence for all shareholders
Executed SaaS subscription and payment processing agreements (Stripe Billing, Direct Debit)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests an enhanced AML review, deliver a board resolution describing the vertical ERP/CRM cloud business model, expected transaction volumes, and a formal low-risk characterization letter from Swiss legal counsel; alternatively, transfer operations to a more technology-friendly cantonal bank.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for ISIC 6201 – office-based vertical software services; no industrial manufacturing or Gewerbegesetz license is required for code development, SaaS hosting, or CRM/ERP cloud operations.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No statutory operating permit required; the AG operates under its Commercial Register entry and must maintain compliant office premises, data protection registration per the revised Federal Act on Data Protection (nFADP), and valid domain/telecom registrations as applicable.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN / BAFU / OFEV), with enforcement by cantonal environmental agencies.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – no full EIA or environmental registration required for office-only software activity; the project is not listed under Annex II of the Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (UVPV / OEIE).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No wastewater discharge or VOC emission thresholds apply to office-bound code development. Compliance obligations: segregated waste disposal under the Federal Waste Ordinance (VVEA); e-waste (servers, laptops) through certified recycling channels; data center hosting, if any, should follow the EU Code of Conduct for Energy Efficiency and Swiss energy ordinances (EnV).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the cantonal fire insurance body (Gebäudeversicherung) for the office premises; workplace occupancy approval under Art. 6 of the Swiss Labour Law (ArG) for any physical office; SUVA occupational health and safety self-control program, including ergonomic workstation assessment and accident prevention protocols; civil defense shelter obligations are not triggered unless employee headcount exceeds the cantonal threshold (typically not relevant for software startups).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung ESTV / Administration fédérale des contributions AFC / Amministrazione federale delle contribuzioni AFC), portal: www.estv.admin.ch / eVAT portal for VAT filings; UID Register maintained by the Swiss Federal Statistical Office / UID registration system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident foreign entity that carries out taxable supplies in Switzerland must first obtain a Swiss UID (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer / Identificateur d'entreprise / Identificatore d'impresa). The foreign entity registers for VAT through the Swiss Federal Tax Administration's eVAT portal using Form 'Registration of a taxable person', accompanied by an official excerpt of the foreign commercial register, articles of incorporation, proof of the principal place of business, and a Swiss tax representative mandate if required. Upon acceptance, the FTA assigns a UID with a separate MWST-VAT number, which serves as the VAT identification number for invoicing and refund purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Switzerland has no US-style check-the-box pass-through election. A Swiss Aktiengesellschaft is invariably taxed at the entity level on worldwide income in Switzerland subject to territorial allocation rules and tax treaties. Available tax elections relevant to the AG include the election to form a VAT group under Article 52 of the Swiss VAT Act, the election to waive VAT exemption on voluntary supplies (e.g., option to tax real estate under Article 22 VAT Act), and election to apply simplified accounting methods for input VAT deduction in certain sectors. Hybrid mismatch elections are not available in Swiss domestic law; however, Swiss anti-hybrid rules apply to neutralise double non-taxation effects.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT / MWST / TVA / IVA) under the Swiss Federal Act on Value Added Tax (VAT Act, 641.20)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 net taxable worldwide turnover per calendar year for Swiss-resident taxable persons; CHF 100,000 net taxable turnover from Swiss supplies for foreign-based undertakings with no Swiss place of business, calculated on a calendar-year basis. Exempt persons may opt-in at any time. For postal and low-value imports a separate registration may be required for foreign distance-selling suppliers above CHF 100,000.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Switzerland does not operate a mandatory real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping system for standard B2B/B2C invoicing. Invoices must contain the mandatory data set defined in Articles 26 and 27 of the VAT Act, including the supplier's UID/VAT number, beneficiary name, invoice date, nature of supply, consideration, and applicable VAT rate. Electronic invoices (e-invoices, PDF/A with XML data, Swiss eBill, QR-bill, and ZUGFeRD/Factur-X-style formats) are accepted, but the original machine-readable file must be retained for audit purposes. Processing and filing of VAT returns is performed via the eVAT online portal, which is the technological clearance point for periodic tax returns and VAT refund applications.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The 0% rate applies to the export of goods where the supplier transfers the power of disposal to the foreign buyer and the goods demonstrably leave Swiss customs territory; the export must be evidenced by a valid customs declaration and transport documents. For services, zero-rating applies when the place of supply is outside Switzerland, particularly B2B services supplied to a foreign-based enterprise, or B2C services effectively used abroad. Vertical ERP and CRM cloud services delivered electronically to non-resident customers generally fall outside Swiss VAT scope or qualify for export zero-rating where the place of supply is located abroad; the supplier must retain evidence of the customer's foreign residence, contract, and actual payment from abroad.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Swiss customs exit declaration / ATS or NCTS message) proving physical export of goods
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, CMR waybill, or other transport document evidencingcross-border movement
Commercial invoice and sales contract identifying the foreign purchaser
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank payment statement evidencing receipt of consideration from abroad
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Swiss Federal Tax Administration conducts risk-based post-clearance audits of zero-rated exports and may require production of all underlying documents. If the required export proof is not complete, credible, and internally consistent, the tax authority denies the 0% treatment and reassesses VAT at the applicable standard rate, with default interest from the original due date. Intentional or negligent documentary falsification or fictitious exports trigger VAT evasion proceedings under Articles 96 to 102 of the VAT Act, leading to penalties of up to three times the evaded tax, criminal fines, and publication of the sanction. The statutory limitation period for prosecution of VAT evasion is generally 10 years. Additionally, the input VAT deduction related to the failed export is clawed back retrospectively, and further penalties apply for missing or false records.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB) – Schweizerische Nationalbank / Banque nationale suisse / Banca Nazionale Svizzera
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland maintains full currency convertibility under the Federal Act on Currency and Payment Means (Bundesgesetz über die Währung und Zahlungsmittel). There is no legal distinction between capital account and current account transactions; no exchange control, no approval requirement, no repatriation or surrender obligation applies to foreign-currency receipts or investments. Profit remittances such as dividends, royalties, and service fees are freely transferable in any currency, subject only to corporate and withholding tax compliance. The Swiss National Bank does not exercise licensing discretion over individual transactions or payment flows and imposes no quantitative restrictions. Practical hurdles to profit remittance may arise solely from bank counterparty due diligence and from Swiss withholding tax at 35% on dividends and analogous distributions, which can be reduced under treaty or exemption procedures.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Swiss law does not require exporters to surrender, convert, or repatriate export proceeds within any statutory timeline. There is no mandatory conversion ratio; proceeds may be retained in any foreign currency in onshore or offshore accounts of the exporter. However, resident enterprises with large cross-border assets or liabilities are subject to statistical reporting obligations to the SNB for the Swiss Balance of Payments and International Investment Position. In particular, companies with annual turnover exceeding CHF 500,000 must file periodic reports (K1/K2 categories) through the SNB electronic reporting facility. Failure to file accurate reports is an administrative violation, not an FX restriction.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low as a primary treasury infrastructure; acceptable only as a complementary payment rail. The Swiss banking regime requires a licence under Art. 1 of the Banking Act 1934 for accepting deposits from the public professionally, and a FinIA licence for financial market activities. Offshor e-money institutions (EMIs) domiciled in the EU cannot passport into Switzerland because Switzerland is not an EEA member state. An overseas digital EMI may provide non-deposit payment services into Switzerland only through a Swiss-licensed correspondent or by obtaining a fintech banking licence under Art. 1b BankG (authorisation cap of CHF 100 million in deposits). For a CH_AG vertical CRM SaaS entity, the practical approach is to pair a Tier-1 Swiss bank account as the operational reserve and treasury anchor with digital EMI accounts (e.g., Stripe, Airwallex, or Currencycloud) for collection and disbursement in foreign jurisdictions, provided the EMI's own KYC/AML controls are at least FATF-equivalent and contractual terms do not create unlicensed deposit-taking in Switzerland.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Swiss banks apply a strict combination of statutory identification under the Anti-Money Laundering Act (GwG/AMLA) and bank-specific organisational instructions. For the CH_AG holding a corporate account with non-resident shareholders or directors, the compulsory KYC interview requires the beneficial owner and at least one director with authorised signature to be physically present at the bank's branch or at a notarially commissioned agent (e.g., a Swiss notary or a licensed Swiss trustee). Several Tier-1 banks allow fully remote opening via video identification using the Swiss Post eID-compliant process or a recognised Swiss video-identification solution for low-risk EU residents; however, for a foreign-controlled AG in the software sector, most compliance officers nevertheless mandate a physical first meeting at the corporate banking desk in Geneva, Zurich, or Zug. Remote opening can reduce the timeline to 2-3 weeks; physical appearance is recommended for controlled, high-value clearing relationships to reduce compliance friction. The bank will require Swiss registered records to be presented as original or certified copies and a power-of-attorney form if a local agent signs on behalf of absent directors.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial owner domiciled in a FATF high-risk or strategically deficient jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Approval documentation pack: (1) Form A beneficial ownership declaration with full chain to ultimate individuals; (2) audited parent company financial statements; (3) FATF/MONEYVAL mutual evaluation report of the owner's home jurisdiction; (4) notarised Swiss board resolution confirming substantive management and commercial rationale in Switzerland; (5) source of wealth affidavit supported by third-party valuation; (6) signed AML statement demonstrating no senior political exposure; (7) Swiss company register excerpt (Handelsregister) showing a physical registered office and actual director list.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Crypto Valley / Web3 affiliation flag for a software company in Zug
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The full dossier must demonstrate that the firm is an ISIC 6201 ERP/CRM provider and not a virtual-asset service provider. Include: (1) detailed business plan and product interface documentation; (2) audited financial statements proving revenue from conventional recurring cloud licences; (3) exclusion of any payment or settlement involving virtual assets (statement signed by all directors); (4) evidence that the firm's banking counterparties are exclusively licensed Swiss or EU institutions; (5) if any DLT-linked experimental branch exists, separate entity documentation and a Swiss DLT law (Distributed Ledger Technology Act) assessment showing no banking activity; (6) transaction list for any prior crypto-related invoice, if any, with legal opinion that sale of software tokens is not a securities issuance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Shell indicator: no visible employees, no office rental, sole function as holding / invoicing hub
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Economic substance package: (1) 12-month Swiss office lease agreement with full furnished premises; (2) payroll records for at least two part-time Swiss employees or a Swiss payroll agent; (3) director movement and attendance logs showing intra-Swiss board meetings at least semi-annually; (4) operational bank statements showing payroll and recurring vendor payments from Switzerland; (5) client contracts referencing the Switzerland-based contractual counter-party; (6) local value objections evidenced by tax filings (VAT, corporate income tax) and social insurance registrations; (7) if the company uses shared services, an arm's-length service and sub-licence agreement with an international group AG.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual trading corridors or customer jurisdictions inconsistent with vertical cloud software
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Counterparty compliance package: (1) sanctions screening audit output from SWIFT or an independent screening vendor for each counterparty; (2) end-user and export control certification for software licences and remote access; (3) contract set including hardware/software licences, maintenance and subscription agreements; (4) beneficial ownership information of each customer if above EUR/CHF 25,000; (5) invoice background and purpose description for any unusual lump-sum; (6) email trail from customer's legal entity resolving the commercial need and payment schedule; (7) no proceeds originating from shell banks; (8) written AML declaration by customer confirming no use of third-country counts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital injection from a holding structure lacking transparent source of funds or without documented equity reason
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Capital transaction record: (1) notarised Swiss capital increase minutes recorded in the commercial registry; (2) share subscription agreement stating the exact amount and consideration; (3) bank statement from the investor remitting the funds; (4) source of wealth evidence of the investor (tax returns or audited group accounts); (5) group organisational chart showing the CH_AG as a genuine operating subsidiary; (6) transfer pricing documentation for any intercompany contribution and loan agreement; (7) legal opinion by a Swiss attorney on capital duty and stamp duty; (8) declaration that the capital is used for ERP/CRM development and not for financial investment.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity and shareholder loan injections must be routed through SWIFT MT103 (or equivalent correspondent clearings) with explicit purpose codes and documentation. For equity contributions, the bank will require a CORPORATE ACTION reference and a narrative describing 'Share Capital Contribution – Art. 630 ff. CO / Swiss capital increase'. Recommended purpose code fields: 'C901 – Capital transfer' in the customer-to-bank instruction; SWIFT P3 category type 'CASH'; and element 72 with reference 'CAPITAL INCREASE / NOTARIAL MINUTES' to prevent erroneous classification. Shareholder loans should use code 'L901 – Intercompany loan' and be supported by a written loan agreement, maturity schedule, and group treasury policy. The verification bundle for any inbound capital injection includes: (1) notarised board minutes and shareholder resolutions approving the contribution; (2) entry in the Swiss commercial register for the paid-up capital; (3) audited or unaudited financial statement demonstrating genuine use of funds; (4) confirmation that the transaction does not trigger Swiss withholding tax (capital contributions are not subject to WHT, while shareholder loans must avoid recharacterisation as 'lending business' under Circular DWSF 2023); (5) proof of the origin of funds from the ultimate shareholder and evidence that funds are transferred solely from that shareholder's bank account. For a vertical cloud AG, the optimal route is a one-time SWIFT MT103 from the parent treasury with advance notice to the Swiss account officer.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For trade and operating disbursements, the primary clearing rails are (1) SWIFT MT103 as irrevocable single-member transfer for ordinary vendor payments, software subscription reseller commissions, and payroll; (2) Commercial Letters of Credit (LC) incidental for cross-border projects where invoicing involves large implementation milestones and customer supply chains; (3) SEPA direct debit for collection from EU-end customers (since Switzerland is part of the SEPA zone, despite not being an EU member, using a Swiss bank with SEPA BIC ensures euro settlement at competitive cost); (4) batch payments using the SIC and euroSIC clearing systems for domestic and pan-European settlement. For outbound disbursement compliance, each payment must carry a legitimate business purpose code; goods or services invoices must match the purpose code (e.g., 'B202 – Payment for IT services'); and for transactions > CHF/EUR 50,000, the bank will request underlying contracts, invoices, and, for export, the export declaration. Commercial LCs are typically used only when the customer is in a jurisdiction with non-convertible currency or high political risk; in such cases, Swift MT700 advice must include full compliance with UCP 600, and the advising Swiss bank will be UBS, ZKB, or another SWIFT member.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: OTC FX forwards (deliverable, with benchmark tenor up to 12 months, documented under ISDA 2002 Master Agreement)
FX options (plain vanilla calls/puts) entered into with Swiss-licensed banks or EEA investment firms with passported rights
Cross-currency swaps and cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) for multi-currency treasury optimisation
Currency swaps executed under an ISDA-CSA framework with daily margin posting
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) strictly limited to genuine commercial exposure in non-convertible or offshore-pegged currencies
CLS-eligible spot FX transactions for same-day settlement risk elimination

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Swiss corporate income and capital tax return (Steuererklärung juristische Personen) covering federal, cantonal and communal taxes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Administration (Kantonale Steuerverwaltung) acting for the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary rule for a 31 December balance-sheet date: ordinance deadline is 15 March in Vaud and Geneva, 31 March in Zurich, and 30 April in Zug; written extension of 1-3 months routinely granted; filing covers the preceding 12-month fiscal period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Cantonal late-filing fine up to 30% of assessed tax when the authority decides ex officio; statutory default interest of at least 4.5% p.a.; forced third-party assessment (Ermessensveranlagung) and criminal tax-proceeding exposure up to CHF 3,000 plus re-assessment for willful omission

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT return (Mehrwertsteuerabrechnung) under the annual settlement scheme available for turnover up to CHF 500,000
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV), VAT Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the end of the tax period; for a 31 December close, the annual return is due by approximately 1 March of the following year, and quarterly filers remain due 60 days after each quarter end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest of 4.5% p.a. on late VAT; late-filing penalty of CHF 100-1,000; administrative fine up to CHF 250,000 and recovery of 1-3 times the evaded tax where intent is proven; refusal to file triggers a third-party estimated assessment

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval of annual financial statements, audit report and discharge resolutions at the ordinary shareholders' meeting (Ordentliche Generalversammlung)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders (internal approval); the documents are not filed with the Commercial Register for non-listed AGs, only register-triggering resolutions are published
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: AGM must be convened within 6 months of the balance-sheet date; for a 31 December year-end, by 30 June of the following year (Art. 699 para. 2 CO); notice of meeting is at least 20 days prior
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Personal liability of the board of directors for loss caused by late convocation; the Commercial Register office may admonish the company and, upon persistent default, request court-ordered enforcement measures including liquidation in extreme cases

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial Register mutation filings covering AGM-resolved changes (board re-elections, registered address, capital events)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) with publication in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SOGC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Any registration-triggering change must be filed within 14 days of the resolution date (Art. 16 para. 1 HRegV); an annual filing is required only if a register-relevant change occurred
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Rectification orders plus compliance fines of up to CHF 900; unregistered changes remain ineffective against third parties in good faith, and the board remains exposed to administrative measures

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual refresh of the internal register of beneficial owners and share register (Aktienbuch) prior to share transfers recorded at the AGM
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Board of directors (internal registers kept at the registered office); disclosure to the Money Laundering Reporting Office (MROS) and criminal authorities upon request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Continuous obligation: beneficial owners holding 25% or more of shares or voting rights must notify the company within 10 days of any qualifying change; reconciliation with transfer books is mandatory at each AGM and before any share transfer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of up to CHF 500,000 for deliberately false or omitted beneficial-owner entries (Art. 697n CO); directors additionally exposed for breach of AML due-diligence duties

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal withholding tax statement and payment (Verrechnungssteuerabrechnung) triggered by any dividend distribution resolved at the AGM
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV), Withholding Tax Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Event-driven: declaration and payment due within 30 days after the payable date of the dividend resolved at the AGM; no obligation in years without distribution
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The 35% anticipatory tax is collectible on the gross distribution; default interest of 4.5% p.a. plus late-payment penalty up to CHF 1,000 per offence; concealment may trigger criminal sanctions against responsible officers

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Ordinary audit (Art. 727 CO) is mandatory when an AG exceeds two of three thresholds for two consecutive years: balance-sheet total CHF 20 million, turnover CHF 40 million, or annual average of 250 full-time positions. A limited audit is required for all other AGs unless the company validly opts out (fewer than 10 average full-time employees, unanimous shareholder consent, no listed status, and no group audit link, Art. 727a CO); opt-out cannot override a shareholder holding at least 10% of votes who requests a limited audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Statutory individual accounts under the Swiss Code of Obligations (Art. 957-963b CO); IFRS or Swiss GAAP FER mandatory for consolidated accounts of listed groups (Art. 962a CO) and permissible for voluntary consolidation; tax reconciliation of book-to-tax differences is filed with the return

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Art. 697j CO, any natural person holding 25% or more of shares or voting rights, or exercising comparable economic control, must notify the AG in writing within 10 days of qualifying; the board records the entry in the internal register of beneficial owners. No external annual UBO filing is yet due for AGs; the annual AGM reconciliation substitutes as the confirmation protocol and the register must be presented to MROS or prosecuting authorities on demand.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of directors and auditor (if elected)
Minute book of shareholders' and board meetings (minutes retained 10 years)
Business books, vouchers and accounting records (retention 10 years)
Audit report when a limited or ordinary audit is performed

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $1,800-$5,500 per year in Zurich or Zug covering domicile address, mail forwarding, statutory register custody, and corporate secretarial calendar management
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $3,500-$11,000 for a limited audit of a small vertical-cloud AG; $17,000-$45,000 for an ordinary audit; $0-$3,000 for an audit opt-out review

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 8.5% federal statutory rate on net profit (effective federal rate ~7.83% as the federal tax is deductible); combined federal and cantonal/communal effective rates range from ~11.9% (Zug) to ~21% (Geneva), with a typical national average of ~14.7%
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Participation relief for qualified dividend income on shareholdings ≥10% held ≥1 year; R&D super deduction of up to 150% of qualifying R&D personnel costs in progressive cantons; patent box capping taxable qualifying IP income at 10% (90% exemption); notional interest deduction (NID) on excess qualifying equity in certain cantons; privileged holding and domiciliary company statuses abolished as of 1 January 2020 under TRAF

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Combined Cantonal and Federal Direct Tax Return for legal entities (Steuererklärung juristische Person / Formulaire pour personnes morales), submitted via the cantonal e-filing portal (e.g., eTax) and transmitted to the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Statutory deadline generally within 6 months after the business year-end; extension to 12 months (typically 31 December of the following year) is granted when the return is prepared by a licensed Swiss tax representative or statutory auditor

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box/Line: Net profit per financial statements (Reingewinn)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Commercial net income shown in the statutory profit and loss account and balance sheet
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Swiss branch or permanent establishment (PE), report only the Swiss-source PE profit; attach the PE accounts and reconciliation to the foreign head-office accounts

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-backs of Swiss federal and cantonal income taxes, capital taxes, excessive board remuneration, portions of entertainment expenses, and depreciation on self-created goodwill
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident entities must add back Swiss taxes levied at source on Swiss-source income; no deduction for deemed interest on equity capital

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduction of qualifying dividend income from a subsidiary in which the company holds at least 10% of the nominal capital for at least one year
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Available only on dividend income attributable to a Swiss PE of a non-resident; no participation relief on the foreign head office's non-Swiss income

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box/Line: Patent box, R&D deduction, NID (kantonale Abzüge)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cantonal preferential deductions on qualifying IP-derived net profit, additional R&D staff costs, and notional interest on qualifying additional equity
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim at cantonal level for the Swiss PE's tax base; attach patent registrations, R&D payroll schedules, and the equity computation memorandum

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Current-year taxable profit reduced by prior-year tax losses brought forward, not exceeding 7 consecutive assessment years
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only losses economically attributable to the Swiss PE may be carried forward; accumulated losses of the foreign head office are not deductible

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: procedural fines and default assessments (typically CHF 20–CHF 500 per day of delay depending on canton); late payment: annual interest of approx. 4.5% on federal tax arrears; negligent incomplete filing: fine of up to CHF 10,000; tax evasion: fine up to 3× the evaded federal tax plus cantonal surcharges; failure to withhold and remit Swiss withholding tax: strict personal and corporate liability for the full 35% tax plus interest

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% Swiss federal withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) on the gross amount of all dividends and other profit distributions paid by a Swiss Aktiengesellschaft
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The 35% statutory WHT operates as a tax-at-source with a refund mechanism: the non-resident beneficial owner applies to the ESTV/FTA for partial or full refund after payment, using the prescribed Swiss WHT refund form, attaching a tax residence certificate (TRC) from the treaty state, the dividend payment voucher, evidence of beneficial shareholding, and an undertaking of beneficial ownership; reduced treaty rates typically 0%–15% depending on DTA and shareholding threshold; refund processing normally 6–12 weeks; advance approval is not required except where the DTA stipulates conditional exemption at source
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 0% domestic Swiss WHT on license fees paid to non-residents; interest: 0% domestic WHT on ordinary intercompany loans and bank debt; the 35% WHT applies only to interest on bonds, convertible loans, and certain book-entry debt securities issued to non-residents (abolished for bank/non-bank debt claims as of 1 January 2022 under TRAF reform)

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Statutory OECD-aligned Master File and Local File required for Swiss entities forming part of a multinational group with consolidated group revenue exceeding CHF 400 million (BEPS Action 13 implementation); below this threshold documentation is not mandatory but contemporaneous TP documentation is strongly recommended to defend the arm's length result; Advance Pricing Agreements (APAs) are available from the Federal Tax Administration
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland does not maintain a formal Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) statute similar to OECD offshore centres; however, substantive economic substance is enforced through the OECD Multilateral Instrument (MLI) Principal Purpose Test (PPT), Swiss anti-abuse case law, and the TRAF 2020 abolition of privileged holding/management/domicile company regimes; a Swiss AG must demonstrate genuine local presence—physical office, operating payroll, locally exercised management and decision-making—to access DTA benefits, participation relief, and to avoid requalification as a sham or mere booking entity

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate or negligent filing of incomplete, inaccurate, or false statements, false books and records, suppression of Swiss-source income, or concealment of taxable profit
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine of up to 3× the amount of federal tax evaded; additional cantonal/communal fines of 100% of the evaded tax; the underlying tax remains due with default interest; no criminal conviction for purely unintentional omissions if corrected immediately in certain cantons
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Board members and beneficial owners can be held jointly and severally liable for unpaid corporate taxes, subjected to civil restitution, travel bans, and imprisonment of up to 3 years in aggravated cases of tax fraud

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Use of forged, falsified, or materially deceptive documents (e.g., fabricated invoices, sham intermediary contracts, or off-shore shell structures) to deceive the tax authorities and conceal tax liability
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine of up to CHF 250,000; imprisonment of up to 3 years; forfeiture of unlawful profits; loss of amnesty protection; duration of penalty assessment extended
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Criminal conviction of the responsible directors, officers, and ultimate beneficial owners; cross-border arrest warrants and extradition; mandatory restitution of unpaid taxes with interest from personal assets

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Swiss AG maintained with no physical office, no genuine local management, no operative employees, passive booking of foreign IP or intercompany service flows, or treaty-shopping arrangements intended solely to obtain artificial DTA benefits
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty relief and refund of the 35% withholding tax (MLI PPT); disallowance of participation relief and patent-box benefits; requalification of sham transactions as constructive dividends subject to WHT; reassessment with 5-year limitation period; penalties up to 3× evaded tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors exposed to personal liability for unpaid withholding tax; civil claims by the Swiss tax administration for restitution; revocation of Swiss residence and work permits for foreign directors; exclusion from future directorship positions

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to deduct, declare, or remit the 35% Swiss WHT on dividends, bond interest, or deemed profit distributions (including shareholder loan waivers, excessive shareholder interest, and non-arm's length payments made to shareholders)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The corporation is held strictly liable for the full 35% WHT on the gross amount, even if no tax was withheld from the beneficiary; default interest at approx. 4.5% p.a.; procedural fines of up to CHF 10,000; the tax claim has preferential rank over ordinary unsecured creditors in bankruptcy
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Statutory personal liability of the board for WHT remittance; personal assets of directors can be seized for the unpaid WHT; criminal imprisonment of up to 3 years for fraudulent concealment of distributions; shareholders may be ordered to repay the net distribution in the liquidation process

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML and Compliance Red Flags (AMLA, Sanctions, PEP)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operation without verified beneficial ownership records, acceptance of unexplained cash or third-party payments, invoicing through shell entities in high-risk jurisdictions, involvement of politically exposed persons (PEPs) or sanctioned states without enhanced due diligence, or use of the company as a conduit for client funds in the ERP/cloud billing cycle
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines of up to CHF 500,000 for regulated entities under the Swiss Anti-Money Laundering Act (AMLA); freezing of bank accounts; mandatory reporting to the Money Laundering Reporting Office (MROS); withdrawal of business licenses; dissolution of the company for serious or repeated violations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers personally liable for AML breaches; criminal imprisonment of up to 5 years for money laundering; confiscation of stolen or laundered assets; travel bans; prohibition from serving as a director in any Swiss company; inclusion on international financial sanctions lists
